title: Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad equation in different bases: application to driven-dissipative two- and multilevel systems
authors: O. A. Ilinskaya, O. V. Ivakhnenko, A. I. Ryzhov, O. Yu. Kitsenko, S. N. Shevchenko
abstract: An open quantum system can be described by a master equation, of which one of the most popular is the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) equation. We revisit description of driven-dissipative quantum systems focusing on the appropriate choice of the system's basis and the respective transformations. We consider the GKSL equation in different bases and calculate the dynamics for a qubit and for a qudit. An appropriate choice of the basis is a fundamental problem for theoretical consideration of open quantum systems and provides an opportunity to obtain the desired evolution in practice.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive review of applying the GKSL master equation to driven-dissipative quantum systems. It argues that the choice of basis—such as diabatic versus instantaneous eigenbasis—is critical because it dictates the correct form of dissipation operators. The work analyzes how different bases must be used for qubits and qudits to accurately model complex, time-varying quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the correct mathematical framework for describing open quantum systems, specifically by choosing the appropriate basis when applying the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation.
main_result: The choice of basis (e.g., diabatic vs. instantaneous eigenbasis) fundamentally dictates the correct form of the collapse operators and thus the resulting quantum dynamics for driven-dissipative systems.
method: The authors analyze the GKSL equation by transforming it into different bases—including diabatic, instantaneous eigenstate, superadiabatic, and Floquet bases—and comparing the resultant equations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on driven-dissipative two- and multilevel quantum systems, exemplified by a qubit (and generalized to qudits) subjected to time-dependent Hamiltonians and dissipation channels.
key_observables: System density matrix ($ho$), energy eigenvalues ($E_{\pm}(t)$), and the dynamics governed by the master equation coefficients.
important_parameters: Driving parameters like detuning ($\Delta, \epsilon(t)$), dissipation rates ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_\phi$), and adiabaticity parameters ($\delta$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on fundamental constraints for master equations (Markovianity, complete positivity) and utilizes approximations such as the Born-Markov approximation or adiabatic expansions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates energy level diagrams in various bases (diabatic, instantaneous, etc.) as a function of detuning; Table I summarizes the basis choice importance.
paper_structure: The paper systematically reviews the derivation constraints for the GKSL equation, applies this formalism to time-dependent Hamiltonians, and details how different unitary transformations are required to correctly map dissipation operators into various physical bases.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it addresses a foundational methodological challenge in open quantum systems theory: ensuring that theoretical descriptions remain physically consistent regardless of the mathematical basis chosen for computation.
